body:
# Phase directive — «`viola focus`» (Epoch 5, viola-0.2.0; the head entry `chk-fw7hhw4r` at `081d4604`)

**WHAT IS AN INPUT, AND WHAT IS NOT.** Of the folder this directive stands in, the ONLY files you read or snap are
this directive and the relay files a later send names. A fact the plan needs and this directive does not state is
ASKED of the overseer in the P3 block, never looked up.

**The operator is AWAY** (asleep, then at work): raise NO question dialog for him. A fork that is his is written to
`{run_dir}/founder-forks.md` (the question, the options in order with each one's cost, the recommendation marked);
his answer comes later through the overseer. **A boundary widening is never settled by a delegate:** it takes its
most conservative arm, marked PROVISIONAL, when the entry can be built whole on that arm — or the phase stops
there. A technical fork is answered by the overseer's relay at once. **This phase makes NO live start, opens,
moves, focuses or closes NO window, dispatches nothing, sends NO key, and reads nothing of the operator's real
`~/.claude*` — a `viola list` among them: on this host the board runs PATH's real `claude` unless none is
reachable.** In your chat messages name a compiled screen literal, never print it.

## Facts, measured by the overseer 2026-11-24T01:35Z — cite them as this directive's

- The tree at `081d4604` = its upstream (ci#45304187236 green): position 132 records, 0 pending, 1 gated
  (`2026-11-23-viola-open-2`, on R2); coverage of viola-0.2.0 `verified 26/37 · deferred 2 · planned 9`. The
  route's next entry is `chk-fw7hhw4r` «`viola focus`», its hint verbatim: «the session's window raised and its
  workspace shown through Hyprland, by recorded identity or ancestry; a named refusal otherwise». It carries NO
  carry. The capability it can claim is v2-11 «Focus a session's window» (method `e2e`).
- `hyprctl locked` read `true` at 01:35:50Z. Another project builds on this host: a gate red with no failed
  assertion is read against `python3 ~/dev/projects/additional/andromedaV3/andromeda-overseer/docs/tools/hostwatch.py
  read --from <the entry's start> --to <now>` first and never re-run for green; read `df -m /tmp` beside it.
- What the last chunk left, to be RE-MEASURED at HEAD, not copied: the wrapper records `window {address,
  workspace, placement, origin}` under `--origin`; `viola-state`'s ancestry walk (at most 8 parent pids, in
  memory); the seam's requests with a focus-window and a workspace dispatch recorded for 0.56.2; the operator's
  answers W1 · W2 · W3 of that chunk (the ancestry walk and the window on the board are HIS, arm (a)). v2-07 is
  NOT verified: no real window opened by `viola open` has been read. A session started by hand records NO window.

## The directive

1. Scope is the route entry as it stands at `081d4604` and v2-11, nothing wider. Say at P1, clause by clause of
   v2-11's acceptance, what «verified» can rest on HERE: which clauses the fake compositor and the fake agent
   prove, and which need a real window raised on the operator's host. **A live focus changes what the operator's
   screen shows and where his keys go: every live reading of it is his to grant, at the host — name each (what it
   raises, how many times, what it leaves, how the earlier focus is restored or not), and plan the claim GATED on
   it if the fakes cannot carry a clause.** Say whether a no-focus probe exists that reads the same path.
2. **Measurements first, at P3, each a number or a closed word from a test, a no-start and no-window probe, the
   recorded fixtures or the code:** what the seam's two focus-side dispatches are at HEAD (their argv as recorded,
   what the fake replays, whether the recorded address and workspace forms match what `focus` must issue); what
   identity `focus` can read for a session opened by `viola open`, for a hand-started `viola run` (no window
   record — which pid the ancestry starts from, and whether the walk the last chunk built is the same function),
   and for a session whose recorded window is gone; the order of the two dispatches and what each failure leaves;
   every refusal's cause. Say what stays the fake's and unmeasured live.
3. **Forks, each with its options priced and marked his or technical:** the verb's argument surface; the closed
   refusal words, exits and hints, each beside the existing tables; whether a stale recorded address falls back
   to the ancestry or refuses; whether `focus` runs for the wheel's driver, a human, or both, and whether it is
   an MCP tool (a driver session moving the operator's focus is a boundary widening — its conservative arm is
   CLI-only); any new time bound and its value; any new record, field or log line. Say plainly whether one
   implement window holds the entry.
4. **Read the playbook's escalate rows BEFORE the P3 block is written**, so that a boundary widening is named in
   the block's first lines, never found at P4. Search ALL seven masters by the counted literals a row or a test
   pins (the verb table, the help's rows, exit-cause tables, the seam's «product caller» wording, the time-bound
   lists) and by «never», «only», «replays no»; name every reached row with the read-not-reached beside them. A
   time-bound list cell that is full is NOT grown and NOT split by this plan: that question stands as the
   operator's fork F1 of run `2026-11-24T00-26-24Z-wrap` — a new bound is listed in Expected amendments as
   waiting on it.
5. **At P3's END, before P4:** ONE block in `founder-forks.md` — your window, the measurements, every reached
   row, each fork of his with the arm taken PROVISIONAL meanwhile, and whether the entry can be built whole on
   those arms. If it can, go on to P4 without waiting; if a fork of his has no conservative arm that builds, stop
   there and say so in one line.
6. Say what each new record writes to DISK, what outlives a SIGKILL, and what a `focus` lets one session learn or
   change about another's window.
7. Every `gate.py control` has an id of 1–16 characters, its `--timeout S`, and an entry filtered to its guard's
   own cases that builds the whole workspace where the case needs a root binary. Every filter term SELECTS at
   least one test under its layer flag once its step is built. An expect atom must be able to fail; a word that
   may honestly read two ways is a READING (`expect = []`); an after-read of state OTHER actors move is keyed to
   the round leg; no entry asserts a state a later step of the same plan ends. A test that skips prints why.
8. **Any live step the plan holds** names: what it needs ABSENT or PRESENT on disk outside the tree and the
   no-start entry that reads it; a script that closes what it opened on every exit path, found a second way when
   its first reading is empty; every inherited `VIOLA_*` name stripped; every board read with no `claude`
   reachable; a stand-in program that takes the arguments the wrapper puts first; and a rehearsal form that
   cannot reach the capped or focus-changing step. It is fired only on the operator's own word.
9. No mutation run. A test that waits takes a bound under the 20 s lint. Every TEST start runs under a test-owned
   user home. Read `df` before a whole rebuild. A fold is decided at the PHASE. A guard's or the permission
   classifier's refusal is never routed around: stop and tell the overseer. On an account-limit refusal, stop.
10. Call NO scheduled-wake or timer tool. End every process you start; remove no scratch clone by a recursive
    delete — name it on the card. Leaves hold no figure the code states.
11. Run the phase exactly as the letters say, read as they stand. On the P5 card, in one block, verbatim where a
    tool printed it: the union's per-master lines and the `rows-union` line; whether EVERY cited row is in the
    union or its standing list; every `[RETYPED]` line and re-spawn; every non-zero exit, refusal, `UNPARSED` /
    `INDETERMINATE` / `NOT DERIVED` line; every place a letter was wrong or silent.

- **Harness rules consulted:** `.claude/rules/verification-harness.md` — read in full, 26 Session Additions read; the ones applied: 2026-10-20 (the `target/debug/viola` hard link: a live script reads the build's hash right before its start), 2026-11-19 (an expect atom never on a word printed when nothing was read), 2026-11-20 (a non-leg entry never reads what a round writes), and the file's lead sentence (a live stand-in takes the wrapper's leading arguments, every inherited `VIOLA_*` unset, every board read with no `claude` on PATH)
- **Platform issues consulted:** none — no runner-only bullet and no CI-reading entry outside the operator leg (Setup 5a read five greens)

- **External inputs:** `inputs#I1` — the overseer's phase directive for this take-up (scope, away rules, the measured facts of 2026-11-24T01:35Z) · `inputs#I2` — the invocation relay (snap it, no dialog, forks to `founder-forks.md`, no live start, window, dispatch or key)

- `crates/viola-hyprland/src/lib.rs` (full) — the closed `Request` set: five queries and three dispatches. `FocusWindow(Address)` builds `["dispatch", "hl.dsp.focus({ window = \"address:<a>\" })"]` (lib.rs:68-74), `Workspace(WorkspaceId)` builds `["dispatch", "hl.dsp.focus({ workspace = <n> })"]` (lib.rs:75-78). `is_dispatch` is true for both and for the move (lib.rs:107-112). Five closed error words: `unsupported` · `unreachable` · `oversize` · `malformed` · `refused` (lib.rs:129-160)

- `crates/viola-hyprland/src/read.rs` (1-60) — `read(program, request, remove) -> Read {reply, exit, stdout}`, `HYPRCTL_DEADLINE` 5 s (read.rs:22), `None` program reads `Unsupported` with no spawn and no line (read.rs:48-49)

- `fixtures/hyprland/0.56.2/FocusWindow.recorded-1.json`, `Workspace.recorded-1.json` — recorded argv `hl.dsp.focus({ window = "address:0x555a9c521790" })` and `hl.dsp.focus({ workspace = 6 })`, each `exit 0`, `stdout "ok\n"`

- `fixtures/hyprland/0.56.2/Clients.recorded-1.json`, `ActiveWindow.recorded-1.json`, `Workspaces.recorded-1.json` — 11 clients. The focus fixture's address `0x555a9c521790` is one of them, on workspace 6, and is also the recorded active window and workspace 6's `lastwindow`: the recorded set is self-consistent for one focus round on that address
- `fixtures/hyprland/0.56.2/Version.absent-1.json` — the no-instance reply: exit 1, non-JSON stdout

- `src/bin/viola-fake-agent/hyprctl.rs` (full) — the fake replays a recorded fixture only when its `args` EQUAL the argv asked (hyprctl.rs:55-57). Any other argv prints nothing and exits 1 (hyprctl.rs:59), which the seam reads as `unreachable`. Modes: `recorded` · `oversize` · `malformed` · `absent` · `terminal`. `terminal` answers only `-j clients` itself, listing the stand-in foot's pid at `TERMINAL_ADDRESS` `0x555aa16bde50` on workspace 2 (hyprctl.rs:17, 54, 64-74), and replays every other argv from the set. It keeps no receipt of the argv it was asked
- `src/bin/viola-fake-agent/foot.rs` (1-40) — the stand-in foot writes `foot-argv` and `foot-pid` beside itself, then runs its words as its direct child

- `src/cmd/open.rs` (1-300) — `parent_target` (open.rs:235-255) reads the parent's snapshot through `read_snapshot_or_replay`, takes `snapshot.window.address` and `snapshot.pid`, walks `ancestors(pid, ANCESTRY)` (`ANCESTRY` 8, open.rs:33) and calls `target_of` (open.rs:259-276), which returns only the WORKSPACE of the recorded address's client, else of the first ancestor pid's client. A replayed snapshot gives no pid, so no ancestry (open.rs:247). It runs no `same_process` check before the walk. hyprctl is resolved through `run::resolve_program` on the caller's PATH, with the R8 strip's names removed from each read (open.rs:133-140)

- `src/run/window.rs` (1-125) — the wrapper's `window_step` finds its terminal's window by the wrapper's parent pid (`std::os::unix::process::parent_id()`, called from `src/cmd/run.rs:544-557` `open_window`) and records `Window {address, workspace, placement, origin}`. It runs only under `--origin`

- `crates/viola-state/src/liveness.rs` (61-200) — `ancestors(pid, max)` (liveness.rs:61-74) is a sysinfo walk of parent pids, at most `max`, stopping at pid 1; it holds pids only and checks no start time. `same_process` (liveness.rs:90), `live_endpoint`, `without_endpoint` (liveness.rs:127-132), `verify_server`
- `crates/viola-state/src/snapshot.rs` (82-89) — `Window {address?, workspace?, placement, origin}`
- `src/cmd/link.rs` (1-60, 129-143) — the nearest CLI-only verb on a named instance: `client::refuse_untrusted` before any log, then `live_endpoint`, inside `cli.link`
- `src/cmd/mod.rs` (55-200) — `Command` enum and `dispatch`; every named-instance verb gets `cli_sink(&home, &args.name)`
- `src/human/hints.rs` (70-110) — open's two fixed pairs and their literal pin test
- `tests/cli_output_plain.rs` (50-70) — `HELP` literal, five group rows
- `tests/cross_exit_causes.rs` (60-130) — `CAUSES` table and `no_two_codes_share_a_hint`
- `tests/contract_error_bodies.rs` (40-75) — `CLI_DOCUMENTS` rows of open
- `tests/cli_open.rs` (grep of its fns) — open's E2E arms run under the fake hyprctl `terminal` mode with the stand-in foot
- `schemas/diag-line.v1.json` line 77 — the `process-exit` `detail` enum, `terminal-not-found` and `not-live` last
- `tests/contract_diag_schema.rs` (221-222) — the detail-enum case table

- **ancestors** — callers: `cmd/open/parent_target()` at `src/cmd/open.rs:253` (the import at `src/cmd/open.rs:19`) and its own unit test (`crates/viola-state/src/liveness.rs:186-192`). Additive reuse; no signature change.

- **target_of** — name collides with `viola-mcp` `tools/*` (crates/viola-mcp/src/tools.rs:437, 452, 473, 482); the open-owned one is called at `src/cmd/open.rs:254` and by three unit tests (`src/cmd/open.rs:499-514`). If focus shares the lookup, the shared function's callers are these sites.

- **viola_hyprland::read** — product callers `cmd/open/opened()` (`src/cmd/open.rs:139`) and `cmd/run/open_window()` (`src/cmd/run.rs:549`). Neither issues `FocusWindow` or `Workspace`: the two focus-side dispatches have NO product caller at HEAD (only the tap `viola-hypr-tap` `record_dispatch()` at `crates/viola-e2e/src/bin/viola-hypr-tap.rs:173,185` and the seam's own tests). Focus would be their first product caller.
- **crate_edges** — `viola`, `viola-state` and `viola-e2e` → `viola-hyprland`; `viola-hyprland` → `viola-core`. No new crate edge.
- **Closed dispatch argv** (crates/viola-hyprland/src/lib.rs:62-90): only a closed `Address` or an `i32` enters a dispatch, through `format!`, one argv element.

- **Read through a closure seam** (src/run/window.rs:22-28, src/cmd/open.rs:235-239): verb logic takes `&mut dyn FnMut(&Request) -> Result<Reply, HyprlandError>`, so its unit tests serve replies and record the requests asked (window.rs:96-112 `seam`). This is the only place where the ORDER and argv of dispatches can be asserted, since the fake binary keeps no receipt.
- **Named-instance CLI verb order** (src/cmd/link.rs:1-6): `refuse_untrusted` → `client::start` (log) → `live_endpoint`, inside `cli.<verb>`.
- **Fixed refusal pairs** (src/human/hints.rs:78-93) pinned by literal in their own unit test and in `tests/cross_exit_causes.rs` `CAUSES`.
- **Help literal**: a served verb joins a group row of `HELP` (tests/cli_output_plain.rs:55-68) and the `help_lists_only_served_verbs` walk.

- **Exit-cause table**: each new code is one `CAUSES` row with its hint (tests/cross_exit_causes.rs:79-100) and one `CLI_DOCUMENTS` row with its witness (tests/contract_error_bodies.rs:42-75), and joins the schema `detail` enum (schemas/diag-line.v1.json:77) with a `contract_diag_schema` case.
- **Test homes**: root integration tests use the `tests/support/` chain; a test-started `viola run` runs under a test-owned user home; long-lived children are tied.

- **E1. Recorded identity → dispatch argv.** For a snapshot window address `a` that `Address::try_new` accepts, `Request::FocusWindow(a).args()` = `["dispatch", "hl.dsp.focus({ window = \"address:<a>\" })"]`, and for the workspace `w` of `a`'s client in a fresh `clients` read, `Request::Workspace(w).args()` = `["dispatch", "hl.dsp.focus({ workspace = <w> })"]`. The frame is `lib.rs:68-78`, pinned by `request_args_are_the_closed_argv_one_element_each` (lib.rs:259-293). For `a` = `0x555a9c521790` and `w` = 6 these equal the two recorded fixtures' `args` byte for byte, so the fake in `recorded` mode replays `ok\n`, exit 0, for both.

- **E2. Ancestry identity.** For a live wrapper (snapshot pid `p` with `same_process` true), `ancestors(p, 8)` yields `p`'s parent chain (liveness.rs:61-74). A wrapper started by the stand-in foot has the foot's pid first, and in `terminal` mode that pid owns `0x555aa16bde50` on workspace 2. So the ancestry arm finds `0x555aa16bde50`/2, whose dispatch argv no recorded fixture holds: the fake exits 1 → `unreachable`. The ancestry arm's full E2E needs a fake change (below).

- **E3. Recorded window and ancestry coincide for `viola open`.** The window step records the client of the wrapper's PARENT pid (run.rs:553), and that parent is `ancestors(p, 8)[0]`. So for an opened session whose terminal still runs, the recorded address and the first ancestry hit name the same client. The recorded address adds nothing that ancestry does not, except where the terminal's pid no longer owns the window, or the wrapper is not the terminal's direct child. Measured by reading the code, not live.

- **E4. Outside Hyprland.** With no `hyprctl` on PATH, `read(None, …)` gives `Unsupported` with no spawn (read.rs:48-49). With `hyprctl` on PATH and no compositor answering, the recorded no-instance reply is exit 1 → `Unreachable` (`contract_hyprland_read_of_the_recorded_no_instance_reply_is_unreachable`, tests/contract_hyprland_seam.rs:201), and security-plan `decision/hyprctl-read-deadline` says that «a deadline kill or a non-zero exit reads as unreachable». So «outside Hyprland → `unsupported`» holds at HEAD only where no hyprctl is reachable.

- **The seam's two focus-side dispatches at HEAD**: `FocusWindow` and `Workspace` as in E1, recorded for 0.56.2 (both `ok\n`, exit 0). The fake replays them only for the recorded address `0x555a9c521790` and workspace 6. Their forms (`address:` + the closed address, an `i32` workspace) are exactly what focus must issue, and they stay within `decision/hyprctl-direct-spawn`'s two measured Lua forms (`hl.dsp.focus`). No new form is needed.

- **The identity focus can read**: (a) a session opened by `viola open`: the snapshot's `window.address`, re-parsed through `Address`, matched in a fresh `clients` read. (b) A hand-started `viola run`: no window record (`window` is absent without `--origin`). The ancestry starts from the snapshot's `pid` (the wrapper), and the walk is the SAME function open uses, `viola_state::liveness::ancestors`. The matching function differs: open's `target_of` returns a workspace, and focus needs the client (address and workspace), so it needs a sibling or a widened return. (c) A session whose recorded window is gone: its address is in no client, so the lookup falls to the ancestry arm (as open's `target_of` does) or refuses — a fork. A REPLAYED snapshot carries no pid (obs history n=12, `contract/replayed-snapshot/live-fields`), so it has no ancestry arm and no liveness.

- **Dispatch order and what each failure leaves**: lean `Workspace(w)` then `FocusWindow(a)`, as v2-11's requirement states both. A failed first dispatch leaves nothing changed by viola. A failed second dispatch leaves the workspace switched and the window not raised. Neither restores the earlier focus: viola reads and keeps no record of it, and a restore would be a third dispatch on a window viola did not open. What Hyprland 0.56.2 does on `hl.dsp.focus({window})` alone (whether it switches workspace itself), and on a special (negative-id) workspace, is UNMEASURED.

- **Every refusal's cause**: a name that fails `ViolaName` → exit 2 (clap). A strict-modes refusal of the home or instance → exit 21 with the instance pair (link's precedent) or exit 1 (open's) — a fork. Not live (no live endpoint) → exit 21 `instance-dead` / `unwrapped-name` by `without_endpoint` (existing words). No hyprctl on PATH → `unsupported`. A seam failure on any of the up to three reads → its own seam word (`unreachable` · `oversize` · `malformed` · `refused`). No client found by either arm → a new word, e.g. `window-not-found`. The words, exits and hints are forks.

- **What stays the fake's and unmeasured live**: that the dispatches actually raise the window and show its workspace on the operator's screen; that `hl.dsp.focus({window})` on 0.56.2 also switches workspace; the special-workspace case; a footclient/foot-server terminal, whose window pid is the server and not an ancestor; and the reading on a host with `hyprctl` installed outside a Hyprland session.

- **No-focus probe**: no product path reads focus's resolution without dispatching. viola takes no dry-run flag, and a flag would be a new surface. The resolution (clients read plus ancestry plus the recorded address) is exercised without a dispatch only over the fake, in a rehearsal form.

title: A. The verb — `src/cmd/focus.rs` (new), `src/cmd/mod.rs` (keeps design S1–S3; layouts S1, S2; obs S1–S3; security S5, S6; a11y S3)

data.head: ### A. The verb — `src/cmd/focus.rs` (new), `src/cmd/mod.rs` (keeps design S1–S3; layouts S1, S2; obs S1–S3; security S5, S6; a11y S3)

body:
1. `FocusArgs`: one positional `name` through `super::send::parse_name` (a `ViolaName`) and `--json`, nothing else.
   No flag selects an arm, a window or a workspace, and nothing after `--`. Doc lines in the form of `OpenArgs`'
   (src/cmd/open.rs:39-66).

2. `focus(home, args)`, in this order, each refusal ending the verb:
   a. `client::refuse_untrusted(home, &name, json)` (src/cmd/client.rs:24) before anything opens under the home:
      `Some(21)` → exit 21 with the instance pair, or under `--json` the `instance-unreachable` /
      `strict-modes-failed` document, no line written (T1).
   b. `client::start(home, &name)` (src/cmd/client.rs:44): the `cli-<name>.ndjson` role file and its
      `process-start`. Then the canonical home (as open does, src/cmd/open.rs:107).
   c. Under `#[instrument(skip_all, name = "cli.focus")]` with no fields: the liveness read. `live_endpoint` of the
      instance dir gives none → exit 21 with `without_endpoint`'s cause (`instance-dead` · `unwrapped-name`),
      through the same exit-21 writer and the same `process-exit` line `viola link` writes for that refusal
      (src/cmd/link.rs), before any hyprctl read (T7). Then the snapshot through `read_snapshot_or_replay`: only
      `Recovered::Snapshot` with `same_process` true goes on; a replayed or absent one is the same not-live refusal.
   d. `hyprctl` resolved by `run::resolve_program(OsStr::new(viola_hyprland::PROGRAM), &cwd)`, and each read's
      environment stripped by `viola_agent_claude::plan_strip(…).remove`, exactly as open does
      (src/cmd/open.rs:133-140). A resolution failure is `None` → the seam's `Unsupported`, nothing spawned.
   e. The decision itself: `focus_with(read, recorded, chain) -> Result<(), &'static str>` takes the closure seam
      `&mut dyn FnMut(&Request) -> Result<Reply, HyprlandError>` (the pattern of src/run/window.rs:22-28). In order:
      - ONE `Request::Clients` read. A seam error → its code (`unsupported` · `unreachable` · `oversize` ·
        `malformed`); a reply of another kind → `malformed`.
      - The client, by `client_of(windows, recorded, chain)`:
        - the client whose address equals `recorded` AND whose pid is in `chain` (the address-reuse guard, T2);
        - else the client whose pid is the first pid of `chain` that any client holds;
        - else none → `window-not-found`.
        `recorded` is the snapshot's `window.address` only when `viola_hyprland::Address::try_new` accepts it, else
        none. `chain` is `ancestors(snapshot.pid, 8)`, held in memory and never written.
      - When the client's workspace is `Some(w)` with `w >= 1`: `Request::Workspace(w)`. Then
        `Request::FocusWindow(client.address)` (T5). Each dispatch's error → its code (`unreachable` · `oversize` ·
        `malformed` · `refused`). A non-`Dispatched` reply → `malformed`.
   f. Exit 1 refusals go through one `refused(json, code, human)` in the form of open's (src/cmd/open.rs:210-219):
      the fixed pair, or under `--json` `{"v":1,"error":"<code>","detail":null}`; then `run::log_self_exit(1,
      Some(code))`.
   g. Success: `human::write_result` of `<name>  focused`, or under `--json` `{"v":1,"ok":{"name":"<name>"}}`; then
      `run::log_self_exit(0, None)`; exit 0. No address, pid or workspace is printed or logged (T6).

3. `src/cmd/mod.rs`: `Command::Focus(focus::FocusArgs)`, its doc line «Bring the named session's window forward and
   show its workspace on Hyprland», placed after `List`. Its dispatch arm uses `resolved_home` and
   `cli_sink(&home, &args.name)`, as `Open`'s does (src/cmd/mod.rs:117-121).

4. Unit cases in `src/cmd/focus.rs`, each over a closure seam that records the requests asked (the `seam` helper
   form of src/run/window.rs:96-112), named `focus_<subject>_<condition>_<expected>`:
   - `focus_dispatches_the_workspace_then_the_window` — the asked list equals `[Clients, Workspace(6),
     FocusWindow(0x555a9c521790)]` for a recorded window in its chain. Its address and workspace are the recorded
     fixtures'.
   - `focus_client_skips_a_recorded_address_outside_the_ancestry` — a recorded address whose client's pid is not
     in the chain gives the chain's client, or `window-not-found` when the chain holds none.
   - `focus_client_falls_back_to_the_nearest_ancestor_window` — the first chain pid with a client wins, not the
     last.
   - `focus_with_no_client_is_window_not_found_and_dispatches_nothing` — the asked list is `[Clients]` alone.
   - `focus_skips_the_workspace_dispatch_for_an_unread_or_special_workspace` — `None` and `-98` each ask
     `FocusWindow` alone.
   - `focus_maps_each_seam_word_to_its_code` — an rstest table over the clients read's four errors and each
     dispatch's four errors: the code, and no later request asked.
   - `focus_of_an_unparseable_recorded_address_uses_the_ancestry` — a recorded address that `Address::try_new`
     refuses is never matched.
   - `focus_args_take_a_name_and_json_only` — clap refuses a second positional, `--workspace`, and a word after
     `--`.

data.head: ### B. The refusal pairs — `src/human/hints.rs` (keeps design S2, S3; layouts S1; a11y S3)

body:
5. One fixed pair per code: `window-not-found`, `unsupported`, `unreachable`, `oversize`, `malformed`, `refused`.
   - Each is plain ASCII, its hint distinct from every other hint (`no_two_codes_share_a_hint`).
   - No hint names `viola release` (design-system · decision/no-hint-names-viola-release), quotes compositor text,
     or locates anything.
   - `<name>` appears only as the parsed argument.
   - The wording is a planning form with the founder's wording owed (founder-forks F-C):
     - `window-not-found`: `no window of <name> was found` / `start <name> in its own terminal window, or open it
       with viola open`
     - `unsupported`: `no hyprctl on PATH` / `viola focus moves windows on Hyprland; run it in a Hyprland session`
     - `unreachable`: `Hyprland did not answer` / `run hyprctl version to check the compositor answers`
     - `oversize`: `Hyprland's reply passed viola's frame cap` / `viola reads no reply past its frame cap; nothing
       was focused`
     - `malformed`: `Hyprland's reply was not understood` / `check that hyprctl matches the running Hyprland`
     - `refused`: `Hyprland refused to focus <name>'s window` / `the window may have closed; viola list shows <name>`
   - Unit case `focus_pairs_are_the_fixed_lines`, in the form of `open_pairs_are_the_fixed_lines`
     (src/human/hints.rs:100).

body:
9. A `Case` in the form of `tests/cli_open.rs`: the fake agent planted as `claude`, `hyprctl` and `foot` (planted
   first, tests history n=46), under a test-owned user home, every child tied, waits only on logged records
   under `WITHIN`, and the teardown that reads `foot-pid` and ends what the case started (tests/cli_open.rs:161).
   Its cases:
   - `focus_of_an_opened_session_raises_its_recorded_window` — `viola open` under `terminal` mode, then
     `viola focus`. Asserts exit 0, stdout exactly `<name>  focused\n`, stderr empty, and `hyprctl-asked` exactly
     the workspace-2 line then the window line.
   - `focus_of_a_hand_started_session_finds_its_window_by_ancestry` — the stand-in `foot` started directly by the
     test (tied), running `viola --home <h> run <name> -- claude` with no `--origin`. Its snapshot has no `window`,
     and focus raises the stand-in's window, asserted the same way.
   - `focus_with_no_window_of_its_session_is_window_not_found` — a wrapper booted with no `foot` ancestor. Asserts
     exit 1, the fixed pair, and no `hyprctl-asked` line.
   - `focus_off_hyprland_is_unsupported` — no `hyprctl` planted. Asserts exit 1, the `unsupported` pair, and no
     `hyprctl-probe` pair in the log.
   - `focus_with_no_compositor_answering_is_unreachable` — `absent` mode. Asserts exit 1, `unreachable`.
   - `focus_of_a_dead_or_unknown_name_is_unreachable_before_any_hyprctl_read` — an absent instance reads
     `unwrapped-name` and a stopped one `instance-dead`. Asserts exit 21, and no `hyprctl-probe` line.
   - `focus_refuses_a_home_another_user_may_read` — the home at 0750. Asserts exit 21, the instance pair, no role
     file opened, the mode read back as found.
   - `focus_json_documents_are_one_document_each` — the ok document and each exit-1 refusal's document. Asserts
     stdout one line, stderr empty, no ESC, no path, and no address (`0x`) or workspace in either stream.
   - `focus_writes_no_snapshot_or_event_line` — `snapshot.json` and `events.ndjson` byte-identical across a

title: F. The gated live reading — `scripts/r3-focus.sh` (new) (keeps security S1; tests S1)

data.head: ### F. The gated live reading — `scripts/r3-focus.sh` (new) (keeps security S1; tests S1)

body:
15. A script `r3-focus.sh <scratch-root> <viola> [--rehearse]`, in the shape of `scripts/r2-open.sh`: `set -u`, a
    `trap` that closes what it opened on every exit path, and `VIOLA_NAME` / `VIOLA_DIR` / `VIOLA_BIN` unset first
    (test-plan · decision/live-rig-clean-start).
    - Preconditions read first: the scratch root absent below its two homes, `foot` and `hyprctl` on PATH,
      `hyprctl locked` reading `false`, and the build's hash printed right before the first start
      (verification-harness 2026-10-20). Any failure prints `r3: red precondition=<word>` and starts nothing.
    - R3a — one stand-in `foot` window running `<viola> --home <scratch>/hand run r3hand -- claude`, where `claude`
      is the fake agent copied into a scratch bin dir first on that child's PATH: a stand-in that takes the
      wrapper's leading arguments, so no real claude starts. Once `r3hand` is live, `<viola> --home
      <scratch>/hand focus r3hand` once, then `hyprctl -j activewindow` read once. It reads `focused` when the
      active window's address is the client of that foot's pid, else the focus's code or `unread`.
    - R3b — one `<viola> --home <scratch>/opened open r3open -- claude`: ONE claude start under the cap, the real
      CLI, its config the private scratch config the way r2-open.sh isolates it. Then `focus r3open` once and the
      same active-window read.
    - Both windows closed and waited gone. The earlier focus is not restored.
    - Every board read runs with no `claude` on its PATH.
    - Its one verdict line: `r3: <green|red> hand=<word> opened=<word>`, green only when both read `focused`.
    - `--rehearse` runs the same steps over the fake `foot` and `hyprctl` in a scratch bin dir, with the fake agent
      as `claude`. It cannot reach the real compositor or a real claude, and prints `r3: rehearsed …`.

16. The script is never run live by implement; it is fired once, on the operator's word, by the operator entry
    below, and its verdict line is copied to `.andromeda/cache/chunks/2026-11-24-viola-focus/evidence/r3.md`.
17. Lint and format; the block below; the claim stays `implemented` with its gated criterion waiting on R3.
- `src/cmd/focus.rs` — the verb, its decision function over the closure seam, its unit cases
- `tests/cli_focus.rs` — the E2E arms over the fakes
- `scripts/r3-focus.sh` — the gated live reading and its rehearsal
- `src/cmd/mod.rs` — the `Focus` subcommand and its dispatch arm
- `src/human/hints.rs` — six fixed pairs and their pin case
- `src/bin/viola-fake-agent/hyprctl.rs` — `terminal` mode's two focus answers and the `hyprctl-asked` receipt
- `src/bin/viola-fake-agent/test_cases_modes.rs` — the fake's two cases
- `schemas/diag-line.v1.json` — six `detail` words
- `tests/cli_output_plain.rs` — `HELP` and the served-verb walk
- `tests/cross_exit_causes.rs` — six rows
- `tests/contract_error_bodies.rs` — six rows
- `tests/cli_error_bodies.rs` — focus in the per-verb document tables
- `tests/contract_diag_schema.rs` — six cases

The block runs the formatter and the linter; the root binaries' units and the filtered new cases (0 on the untouched
tree, read red-vacuous at baseline); the new integration binary by its cases' prefix; the readers of the moved
literals and tables; the rehearsal of R3 over the fakes; the host read; the harness's three layers; then the operator
pass.

**What is not run, and why:** no round entry — R3 is the operator's act, fired once on his word through the
`operator` entry below, never by implement (`inputs#I2`). No boot smoke: no boot-path file changes (`src/cmd/run.rs`
and `src/run/` are untouched, research §Files to modify). No mutation run (`inputs#I1` item 9). No fuzz target: no
new parser — the clients reply goes through the seam's existing parse. No `cargo deny`: no dependency edge moves
(research §Graph impact, crate_edges).

**The remove-the-guard controls** are implement's one-shot `gate.py control` runs, never entries. Each is fired on
the `ctl-root` entry, its case named, `--timeout 900`; each case fails on its own bounded assertion, so a `timeout`
reading would NOT read the guard as held.
| id | File | The edit removes | Case | Entry |
| `focus-reuse-guard` | `src/cmd/focus.rs` | the `chain` membership test on the recorded arm of `client_of` | `focus_client_skips_a_recorded_address_outside_the_ancestry` | `ctl-root` |
| `focus-order` | `src/cmd/focus.rs` | the `Workspace` dispatch before `FocusWindow` | `focus_dispatches_the_workspace_then_the_window` | `ctl-root` |
| `focus-no-dispatch` | `src/cmd/focus.rs` | the early return on no client | `focus_with_no_client_is_window_not_found_and_dispatches_nothing` | `ctl-root` |

body:
- (product) `viola focus <name>` on a live session opened by `viola open` dispatches, in order, the workspace focus
  of its window's workspace and the focus of its recorded window (only when that window's pid is in the wrapper's
  ancestry), and exits 0 printing `<name>  focused`. Proven over the fakes by
  `focus_of_an_opened_session_raises_its_recorded_window` and `focus_dispatches_the_workspace_then_the_window`
  (architecture · decision/hyprland-seam-crate; security-plan · decision/window-record-kept-to-snapshot-and-event-log).

- (product) For a hand-started `viola run` (no window record), focus finds the window of the wrapper's nearest
  ancestor pid and dispatches the same pair: `focus_of_a_hand_started_session_finds_its_window_by_ancestry`,
  `focus_client_falls_back_to_the_nearest_ancestor_window`.

- (security) A recorded address whose window's pid is not in the live wrapper's ancestry is never focused:
  `focus_client_skips_a_recorded_address_outside_the_ancestry` and its `focus-reuse-guard` control.

- (product) With no window found it refuses `window-not-found`, exit 1, and dispatches nothing; with no `hyprctl`
  on PATH it refuses `unsupported`, exit 1, spawning nothing; with `hyprctl` and no compositor answering it refuses
  `unreachable`; each seam failure refuses with its own word. Cases: `focus_with_no_window_of_its_session_is_window_not_found`,
  `focus_off_hyprland_is_unsupported`, `focus_with_no_compositor_answering_is_unreachable`,
  `focus_maps_each_seam_word_to_its_code` (obs-plan · decision/distinct-detail-code-per-exit-cause).

- (security) A not-live or unknown name refuses exit 21 (`instance-dead` · `unwrapped-name`) and a home another
  user may read refuses exit 21 with the instance pair, each before any hyprctl read and the latter before any log:
  `focus_of_a_dead_or_unknown_name_is_unreachable_before_any_hyprctl_read`,
  `focus_refuses_a_home_another_user_may_read` (security-plan · decision/state-tree-strict-modes-before-use).

- (cli) Each refusal is one fixed pair, or under `--json` one clean document; no output or log line holds a window
  address, pid or workspace; `viola --help` lists `board:    list, focus`. Tables: `cross_exit_causes`,
  `contract_error_bodies`, `cli_error_bodies`, `cli_output_plain`, `contract_diag_schema` green
  (design-system · contract/help-output/verb-groups; layout-templates · contract/viola-help/verb-groups).
- (state) A focus writes no snapshot and no event line: `focus_writes_no_snapshot_or_event_line`.
- (tests) `bash scripts/agent-run.sh run --unit`, `run --integration` and `run --e2e` each print `"ok":true`.

- **`matrix#v2-11`** — GATED on R3: on Hyprland, focusing a named session brings its window forward on its
  workspace, for a session viola opened and for one started by hand. This is read as
  `r3: green hand=focused opened=focused`, the active window after each focus being that session's terminal
  window, in `.andromeda/cache/chunks/2026-11-24-viola-focus/evidence/r3.md` (the gated entry). With no window
  found it refuses with a named cause (`window-not-found`), and outside Hyprland, with no `hyprctl` reachable, it
  refuses as `unsupported` (both proven over the fakes now). A stand-in or recorded artifact never verifies the
  gated part.

- Rows: architecture · decision/hyprland-seam-crate, decision/hyprctl-direct-spawn, decision/human-controls-cli-only,
  contract/cli-exit-codes/1, contract/cli-exit-codes/21; security-plan · decision/hyprctl-read-deadline,
  decision/open-ancestor-walk-in-memory, decision/window-record-kept-to-snapshot-and-event-log,
  decision/state-tree-strict-modes-before-use, decision/window-step-moves-own-terminal-window; design-system ·
  contract/help-output/verb-groups, decision/no-hint-names-viola-release; layout-templates ·
  contract/viola-help/verb-groups, contract/cli-verbs/help; obs-plan · decision/span-naming,
  decision/distinct-detail-code-per-exit-cause, decision/log-schema-additive-only; a11y-plan ·
  decision/time-bounds-never-on-human, decision/time-bounds-fall-on-the-driver; test-plan ·
  decision/window-placement-proven-live, decision/live-rig-clean-start, decision/fakes-for-external-services.

- History: architecture n=1-3, n=7, n=10, n=12; security n=1-3, n=6, n=9; obs n=1-2, n=22; tests n=5, n=7; design n=1-2;
  layouts n=1; a11y n=4 (the run dir's `*-history.md`).

- Research (`doc:2026-11-24-viola-focus/research` rev 2): crates/viola-hyprland/src/lib.rs, src/cmd/open.rs,
  src/run/window.rs, crates/viola-state/src/liveness.rs, src/bin/viola-fake-agent/hyprctl.rs, src/cmd/client.rs,
  src/cmd/link.rs, the 0.56.2 fixtures.

- Forks: `.andromeda/runs/2026-11-24T01-36-38Z-phase/founder-forks.md` (P3 block, F-A to F-D, T1-T7); `inputs#I1`,
  `inputs#I2`.

- An MCP `focus` tool — rejected on the conservative arm of F-A: a driver moving the operator's keys is a second
  widening (architecture · decision/human-controls-cli-only).

- Taking the recorded address unconditionally, as open's `target_of` does — rejected (T2): a gone terminal's
  address can be reused by another window, and a focus would raise a window no viola session owns.

- Remapping a quick non-zero `hyprctl` exit to `unsupported` — rejected (T3): security-plan ·
  decision/hyprctl-read-deadline reads «a deadline kill or a non-zero exit reads as unreachable».

- Detecting Hyprland by an environment read (an instance signature) — rejected: a new environment read needs its
  own Decisions Log entry (security history n=13).
- Printing the window's address or workspace — rejected (T6): a new leave path for the window record.

- Restoring the earlier focus — rejected: a third dispatch on a window viola did not open, from a record viola does
  not keep.

- Changing `src/cmd/open.rs`'s `target_of` — rejected: focus keeps its own stricter matcher, and open's behaviour
  and its three cases stay as they are.
- A new time bound — none: at most three seam reads, each under `HYPRCTL_DEADLINE`.

- The address-reuse guard leans on `ancestors` reading the live wrapper's chain now. Its pids carry no start time
  each, but the wrapper itself is checked by pid and start time first (`same_process`), and a terminal that ended
  would end the wrapper it hosts.

- A footclient (foot server) window belongs to the server's pid, which is no ancestor of the wrapper. Focus refuses
  `window-not-found` there, an honest reading, carried in the report. `viola open` spawns `foot` itself, not
  `footclient`.

- `hl.dsp.focus({window})` alone may already switch workspace on 0.56.2 (unmeasured); the workspace dispatch first
  is harmless where it does and needed where it does not.

- Counts: six new codes (the list in step 5); the root `CAUSES` table grows by six rows (tests/cross_exit_causes.rs@HEAD
  holds 25, by reading lines 79-100).

- Expected amendments (wrap):
  - architecture: `name/command/focus` added; `decision/human-controls-cli-only` names `focus` (PROVISIONAL,
    founder-forks F-A; pattern `rul-r74hshif` Boundary widening, answered by: none yet — the operator's word owed);
    `contract/cli-exit-codes/1` and `/21` name focus's refusals.
  - security-plan: a new row «`viola focus` raises only a live wrapper's own terminal window, found by its recorded
    address within its ancestry or by its ancestry, at most one workspace and one window dispatch, never a window of
    no viola session» (PROVISIONAL, the F-A widening, pattern `rul-r74hshif`, his word owed); a sibling of
    `decision/open-ancestor-walk-in-memory` for focus's walk (that cell names open alone);
    `decision/state-tree-strict-modes-before-use` gains `focus`; `decision/window-record-kept-to-snapshot-and-event-log`
    stands, focus printing none of it.
  - design-system and layout-templates: `contract/help-output/verb-groups`, `contract/viola-help/verb-groups`,
    `contract/cli-verbs/help` gain `focus` in the board row (PROVISIONAL, F-B); the fixed-form verb lists
    (`contract/cli-refusal-line/fixed-unable-form`, `contract/cli-stderr/fixed-message-refusal`) and
    `contract/cli-exit-codes/1` name focus; the six pairs as planning forms (F-C).
  - obs-plan: `contract/process-exit-detail/exit-1` gains the six words; a `contract/cli-log-file/focus` row as
    open's.
  - a11y-plan: a human verb now bears `HYPRCTL_DEADLINE` (up to three reads) — NOT grown into
    `decision/time-bounds-never-on-human` or `decision/time-bounds-fall-on-the-driver` (their cells are full); it
    waits on fork F1 of run `2026-11-24T00-26-24Z-wrap`.
  - test-plan: `decision/fakes-for-external-services` — the fake hyprctl's `hyprctl-asked` receipt and `terminal`

   both (for one, `focus-reuse` and `focus-no-client` fit); `focus-order` stands.

   stand-in and the whole reading is lost. If the letters or a rule of the tree forbid a fake binary beside a
   release-shaped one in a live reading, say so and propose the stand-in the R2 script writes for itself instead.
4. **R3b is a live `viola open`; R2 has not read green.** Say in the R3 gate entry's note and in the report's

A `viola focus <name> [--json]` CLI verb that brings a named live session's window forward and shows its workspace
on Hyprland, through the two focus dispatches `viola-hyprland` already holds and records for 0.56.2
(research §Measurements). The window is found by the live wrapper's own identity. It is the window the wrapper
recorded under `--origin` (`viola open`'s), trusted only when that window's pid is in the wrapper's process
ancestry. Otherwise it is the client of the nearest ancestor pid of the wrapper (a hand-started `viola run`), using
the same `viola_state::liveness::ancestors` walk `viola open` uses. Every other outcome is a named refusal. With no
`hyprctl` reachable it refuses `unsupported`; with `hyprctl` and no compositor answering it refuses `unreachable`, as
the seam reads it — the reading of «outside Hyprland» the plan takes PROVISIONAL, F-E.

      - the stand-in written and its `--version` answered with exit 0 and its fixed line;
      - the build's hash printed right before the first start (verification-harness 2026-10-20).
    - **R3a.** One stand-in `foot` window running `<viola> --home <scratch>/hand run r3hand -- <stand-in>`; no

# Implement directive — «`viola focus`» (chunk 2026-11-24-viola-focus)

The plan is approved (P5 card 2, plan rev 4). This window is fresh: read the chunk's documents from the store and
its evidence dir from disk first. This directive is the only file of its folder you read or snap.

**In your own chat messages never print a compiled screen literal verbatim**: name it. Call no scheduled-wake or
timer tool. **NO mutation run and NO witness run. NO window of the real compositor is opened, moved, focused or
closed, NO dispatch reaches the real `hyprctl`, NO key is sent and NO real `claude` is started by this run — R3 is
not this run's: `scripts/r3-focus.sh` runs ONLY in its `--rehearse` form, over the fakes.** Nothing of the
operator's real `~/.claude*` is read; no `viola list` runs with a real `claude` reachable on its PATH.

## The host — another project works here

- The filtered entries run as they come. **Before the three whole layers (unit, integration, e2e) and again before
  `pre-push`: read `hostwatch.py read --last 15`** (`~/dev/projects/additional/andromedaV3/andromeda-overseer/docs/tools/hostwatch.py`)
  and `df -m /tmp` beside it. QUIET → go on. CONTENDED naming a NEIGHBOUR alive in the stalled seconds → STOP and
  say in one line which entries wait; the overseer arranges a quiet window. A CONTENDED reading where only this
  run's own build was alive is none: go on.
- A gate red where no assertion failed on a value (a stall, a timeout, a kill) is read against the same record
  first and never re-run for green into a contended host: say so and wait for the overseer's word.

## Stops

- **The plan's order is the order.** The rehearsal entry is fired once the script exists and BEFORE any graded
  use: read with your own eyes that its PATH holds the fake `hyprctl`, `foot` and `claude` first and that no line
  of it can reach `/usr/bin/hyprctl` — say how you read it. A rehearsal that reached the real compositor is a
  stop, reported at once.
- **The three controls** (`focus-reuse`, `focus-order`, `focus-no-client`) are fired by `gate.py control` with the
  plan's `--timeout 900` on the `ctl-root` entry. A case that cannot be made to fail with its guard removed stops
  implement for that site.
- **No new closed word, exit, flag, request, time bound, environment read, record field, MCP tool or fake mode
  beyond the plan's:** a need for any stops implement and is the operator's — he is away, so it is written to the
  run's `founder-forks.md` with its options priced and the step stops there.
- A filter that still selects 0 tests after its step is a red, said so. A sweep of a counted literal (the help's
  rows, the exit-cause table's row count, the `detail` enum, the per-verb document tables) reads the test tree's
  strings too.
- A red that would move a plan entry stops implement before the operator pass: say which entry and why.
- A guard's or the permission classifier's refusal is never routed around: stop and say so. On an account-limit
  refusal, stop where you are. Remove no scratch clone or test dir by a recursive delete: name it in the report.
- Every TEST start runs under a test-owned user home and runtime dir, and every test ends the stand-in terminal
  and the wrapper it started. No leaf gains a figure the code states. No master row is reworded in this skill.

## On green — the operator pass, WITHOUT R3

Write the chunk report (P4), saying plainly what stands unproven behind R3 and behind the operator's forks F-A to
F-E. Then run the operator pass in this same window: `pre-push`, hygiene, the pre-CI commit and push, the CI read
(`ci.py conclusion`, leg=operator). **Fire neither the release-shaped build entry nor R3: both wait on the
operator's own word, which has not been given.** Write the pass's record as it stands, R3 unfired, the gated entry
deferred, and end the turn with one line: the CI verdict, the rehearsal's verdict line, and what is left on disk
outside the tree, each by name. End every process you start.

title: 2026-11-24-viola-focus — Threat Model Summary: 1 row(s)
body:
## 2026-11-24-viola-focus — Threat Model Summary: 1 row(s)
**Section:** Threat Model Summary
**Change:** ~ decision/state-tree-strict-modes-before-use · rule: was «run, revive's start, open, verify and focus hold the home tree to the strict-modes check before their first read or open under the home and before any log opens; a refusal exits 1, and focus's exits 21 strict-modes-failed.»; now «run, revive's start, open and verify hold the home tree to the strict-modes check before their first read or open under the home and before any log opens; a refusal exits 1.»
**Why:** decision/state-tree-strict-modes-before-use: the row as set at tx 4464 names focus among the home-tree verbs, but focus runs the instance check (client::refuse_untrusted, check_instance) and not check_home_tree, so the row is false for it; its instance check stands on decision/cli-frame-verbs-strict-modes-first.
**Ref:** .andromeda/runs/2026-11-24T03-08-15Z-wrap/

- CLI exit codes: 0 · 1 (a `cli` verb's internal error: `error: internal error` on stderr, or under `--json` before a `--` the catch site's `{"v":1,"error":"internal-error","detail":null}` on stdout, stderr then empty, `run`, `revive`'s start, `mcp` and `hook` silent at that site; also `viola run`'s and `viola revive`'s start, and `viola verify`, refusing the home tree before any log opens: the home-state `unable:` / `hint:` pair, or the instance-state pair for an instance-level refusal, no line written, no child started; also `viola run` and `viola revive`'s start refusing the socket directory (`socket_dir_ready`, before any snapshot, child or `Server::bind`; a failed create and a refused check read this one code, a `Server::bind` failure does not): the stderr `unable:` / `hint:` pair, or under `viola revive --json` the `socket-dir-refused` document, and one `process-exit{subject:"self", exit_code:1, detail:"socket-dir-refused"}`, no path, pid or uid; `viola verify`'s refusals each carry their code on the `process-exit` it writes under a parsed `VIOLA_NAME`: `program-not-found` · `pinned-hash-mismatch` · `version-unreadable` · `strict-modes-failed` · `unclean-fixture`, beside `interrupted`; a failing row is no refusal and carries no code, yet `viola verify` still exits 1 on a failed relied row with that row's stamp written, and `verify` takes no `--json`; also `viola open`'s refusals, `strict-modes-failed` before any log, `already-live`, `stale-heartbeat`, `pinned-hash-mismatch`, `terminal-not-found`, `not-live` or `internal-error`, each under `--json` the `{"v":1,"error":"<code>","detail":null}` document; also `viola focus`'s refusals, each an `unable:` / `hint:` pair on stderr with no path, or under `--json` one refusal document) · 2 (usage error, and `viola send` text over 16 MiB or not UTF-8) · 10 human-typing · 11 unassigned (the retired `budget-paused` refusal's code, never reused or renumbered) · 12 unverified-cli · 13 not-delivered · 14 unknown · 20 wrapper fault (a `-32602` from `link` / `unlink` included) · 21 instance unreachable (under `--json` `{"v":1,"error":"instance-unreachable","detail":"<cause>"}`, written by `client::unreachable_document` (the board builds its own), `<cause>` one of the six exit-21 words of `viola_core::UnreachableCause`'s closed seven (the seventh, `call-deadline`, written by the MCP frame tools alone) `strict-modes-failed` · `instance-dead` · `unwrapped-name` · `endpoint-lost` · `server-verify-failed` · `socket-dir-refused`, no `RefusalReason`; with no live endpoint `viola_state::liveness::without_endpoint` reads an instance directory as `instance-dead` and anything else as `unwrapped-name`, so a stale instance reads `instance-dead`, and a wrapper lost with the call open reads `endpoint-lost`; also, on `send` / `wait` / `last` / `answer` / `pause` / `release` / `link` / `unlink`, a server that is not the recorded wrapper — a connected peer whose euid is not this user's or cannot be read (`peer_admitted`), or the connected peer's pid or OS start time not the snapshot's, or that check not made — no frame written, `{"v":1,"error":"instance-unreachable","detail":"server-verify-failed"}` under `--json` (Linux only; the Windows and macOS legs left with their code, recoverable at the tag `multi-os-final`), after the client's own exit-13 refusals, the strict-modes instance check and the socket-directory check, with no exit code or `RefusalReason` of its own, its `--json` word the document's `detail`; also `viola list`'s refused strict-modes check of the home, `instances/` or any one instance, which refuses the whole board, no log opened; also `viola focus`'s refused strict-modes check: the `unable:` / `hint:` pair, or `{"v":1,"error":"instance-unreachable","detail":"strict-modes-failed"}` under `--json` with stderr empty, nothing under the home opened and no line written; and `viola plugin install`'s refused strict-modes check of the home or an existing `marketplace/` tree dir, nothing created, no log opened; and the refused instance check of `send` / `wait` / `last` / `answer` / `pause` / `release` (the target instance) and of `viola link` / `viola unlink` (the driven instance), made first by `client::refuse_untrusted` (`check_instance` on the home and `instances/<name>`, after `send`'s text read, before any connect, role file or log opens): the instance-state `unable:` / `hint:` pair, or `{"v":1,"error":"instance-unreachable","detail":"strict-modes-failed"}` under `--json`, no log opened, no line written; and, on those same eight verbs, past that check and before any connect, a refused socket directory on the recorded endpoint (`check_endpoint_dir` in `client::connect`): the socket-directory hint last on stderr, or `{"v":1,"error":"instance-unreachable","detail":"socket-dir-refused"}` under `--json`, one `process-exit` at WARN with `during` `connect` and no `channel-request`); `viola hook` always 0. `viola revive` exits 0, 1 for a refused strict-modes check (ahead of the wrapper log: the stderr pair, no log line) or a preflight refusal (`already-live` or `stale-heartbeat` · `no-session` · `session-live` · `cwd-missing`, read in that order, each one `process-exit` line) or a refusal of the start after a passed preflight, or 2 for a usage error; it takes `--json` on both arms, where a refused strict-modes check and every refusal of its start is instead one stdout document `{"v":1,"error":"<code>","detail":null}` (`strict-modes-failed` · `already-live` · `no-session` · `session-live` · `cwd-missing` · `stale-heartbeat` · `pinned-hash-mismatch` · `squatted-name` · `socket-dir-refused` · `internal-error`, by `client::refused_document`; a `claude` not on `PATH` or an anyhow error of the start is `internal-error`), stderr empty, exit 1, and `<name> --list --json` prints `{"v":1,"ok":{"sessions":[…]}}` in log order (a `pump_child` error prints no document: the child has held the terminal).

- Arguments mirror channel params: `viola send <target>` (text from stdin or `--file`), `viola wait <target> [--after <cursor>] [--timeout-ms <n>]`, `viola last <target>`, `viola answer <target> <dialog_id>` (response JSON from stdin/`--file`), `viola pause <target>`, `viola release <target>` (a `--budget` flag is a usage error, exit 2), `viola link|unlink <driver> <driven>`; `viola open <name> [--parent <name>] [--role overseer|builder|worker] [--cwd <dir>] [--workspace N] [--model M] [--effort E] [--json] -- claude`; `viola focus <name> [--json]` takes one ViolaName and `--json` only; `viola revive <name> [--id <ID>] [--fork] [--model <MODEL>] [--effort <EFFORT>] [-- <child args>]` and `viola revive <name> --list` send no channel frame (`--list` conflicts with `--id`, `--fork`, `--model`, `--effort` and the trailing arguments); `viola run --parent <NAME>` declares the instance's parent (one equal to its own name a usage error, exit 2, before anything is read; with no `--parent` an inherited `VIOLA_NAME` is taken as parent only, dropped when it equals the own name) and `viola run --role <WORD>` its role, a code word; `viola run --model <MODEL>` names the model handed to the child, a model word, and `viola run --effort <EFFORT>` its effort, one of the five effort words, a value failing its shape a usage error, exit 2, and with none given each is the `config.json` default, else the compiled default; the hidden `viola run --origin <WORD>` names the window's origin, an origin word (any other word a usage error, exit 2), and the hidden `viola run --place <N>` the workspace the window is moved to (`--place` without `--origin` a usage error, exit 2).

- Tool inputs: `send {target, text}`, `wait {target, after?, timeout_ms?}`, `last {target}`, `answer {target, dialog_id, response}`, `list {}`. `release`, `pause`, `link`, `unlink` are CLI-only (an affordance, not enforcement); `focus` is CLI-only too: no MCP tool raises a window, and adding one is a boundary widening of its own.

- Strict-modes runs in every process that reads `snapshot.json` or `ledger/stamps.json` (`run`'s and `revive`'s starts and `verify` through `check_home_tree`, `verify`'s `update_stamps` through `check_stamps`, `run`'s version gate through `stamps::read_stamps_strict` (the `strict` module's `check_stamps` first, a refusal `cli_verified:false`), `hook`'s event and dialog paths through `trusted`, the CLI frame verbs `send` / `wait` / `last` / `answer` / `pause` / `release` and `link` / `unlink` through `client::refuse_untrusted`, `viola focus` (a refusal exits 21 `strict-modes-failed`), `viola mcp`'s frame tools through `check_instance`); each existing `events.ndjson` is checked before it is opened.

**Kept:** the «Eight» lead of decision/time-bounds-never-on-human and decision/time-bounds-fall-on-the-driver stays provisional: it is not his word («These»), the `viola up` wrap's W2.
**Ref:** .andromeda/runs/2026-11-24T17-14-08Z-wrap/

- `viola adopt` is refused like `run` when the name is `live` or `stale`, and with `session-live`, exit 1, when a `claude agents --json` row carries the id (a failed read passes); a refusal exits 1, under `--json` the `{"v":1,"error":"<code>","detail":null}` document (`strict-modes-failed` · `session-live` · `already-live` · `stale-heartbeat` · `pinned-hash-mismatch` · `squatted-name` · `socket-dir-refused` · `internal-error`). `viola open <name> [--parent <name>] [--role overseer|builder|worker] [--cwd <dir>] [--workspace N] [--model M] [--effort E] [--json] -- claude` — open a session in its own terminal window (refused like `run` when the name is `live` or `stale`); exit 0 once the session went live (the human line `<name>  live  <placement>`, under `--json` `{"v":1,"ok":{"name","parent","window","placement"}}`, window `{address, workspace}` or null), 1 for a refusal (`strict-modes-failed` · `already-live` · `stale-heartbeat` · `pinned-hash-mismatch` · `terminal-not-found` · `not-live` · `internal-error`, under `--json` the `{"v":1,"error":"<code>","detail":null}` document), 2 for a usage error (a clap error, any word after `--` but `claude` alone, or a parent equal to the opened name). `viola focus <name> [--json]` — raise the named session's window (takes one ViolaName and `--json` only; CLI only, no MCP tool raises a window); exit 1 with one process-exit detail: `window-not-found` (no window of the session, nothing dispatched), `unsupported` (no hyprctl reachable, nothing spawned), `unreachable` (hyprctl reachable, no compositor answering) or the hyprctl seam's `oversize`, `malformed` or `refused`; exit 21 on a refused strict-modes check (under `--json` `{"v":1,"error":"instance-unreachable","detail":"strict-modes-failed"}`, nothing opened, no line written). `viola up [<NAME>...] [--dry-run] [--json]` — after a reboot, re-open each instance gone before the boot through `viola revive` in a new terminal, parents before children (a live or stale instance skipped; an unnamed one ended on purpose stays down; names given narrow the fleet, a name not scanned reads `not-taken`; `--dry-run` spawns nothing; CLI only, no MCP tool); exit 0 when every line reads `live`, `already-live`, `stale-heartbeat` or `would-open`, 1 for any other line or a refusal (`boot-time-unread` · `strict-modes-failed` · `pinned-hash-mismatch` · `terminal-not-found`, under `--json` its document), 21 when its board scan's strict-modes check refuses (`instance-unreachable`, `strict-modes-failed`, no line printed). No `viola ui` subcommand: viola has no web or graphical frontend; its view beyond `viola list` is the keyboard-driven terminal fleet console tiled on Hyprland (matrix#v2-14), owed by the 0.2.0 Epoch 6 route entries «Console scaffold», «Fleet console view» and «Console actions». `viola switch <name> [--model <MODEL>] [--effort <EFFORT>] [--json]` — switch a running wrapped session's model and effort in place, resuming the same session id on the new pair under the same wrapper (at least one of `--model` and `--effort`, else a usage error, exit 2; prints `<name>  switched  <model> <effort>` and exits 0, 10, 12, 13, 14, 20 or 21; CLI only, no MCP tool switches a session's model or effort). `viola mcp [--home <dir>]` — the stdio MCP server (tools `send · wait · last · answer · list`), hidden from `viola --help` and run by the plugin, never by a person: no argument but the global `--home`, it serves until stdin closes or a stdin line passes `MAX_FRAME` (refused whole, never truncated or skipped, with one `parse-rejected{parser:"mcp-stdin", detail:"oversize", count:1}` line holding no byte of it), which ends the session as a close does (exit 0 once initialized, 1 before `initialize`, both streams empty), and exits 1 with nothing on stdout or stderr and no role file when its home or `diagnostics/` fails `viola_state::strict::check_path` (that exit does not block the CLI's start: the session reaches `idle` and the CLI logs the server's connection as failed, measured on claude 2.1.287 on the Linux dev host)

- Log only fields named in obs-plan §6 (default-deny, enforced by G4). `detail` codes are closed kebab-case lists — never a path or pid. The session id an operator types to `viola adopt` never appears in any line, field or detail. `schemas/diag-line.v1.json` closes `process-exit`'s; `viola focus` ends exit 1 with one `process-exit` detail: `window-not-found` (nothing dispatched), `unsupported` (no hyprctl reachable, nothing spawned), `unreachable` (hyprctl reachable, no compositor answering), or the hyprctl seam's `oversize`, `malformed` or `refused`; exit 21's closed causes are `instance-dead`, `unwrapped-name`, `endpoint-lost`, `strict-modes-failed`, `server-verify-failed`, `socket-dir-refused` (`during` `call` for `endpoint-lost` alone; `instance-dead`, `unwrapped-name`, `server-verify-failed` and `socket-dir-refused` are `during` `connect`), and `stale-heartbeat` is exit 1's cause alone (a frame verb against a stale instance reads `instance-dead`). `channel-response` carries `detail` on a `-32602` only (`unsupported-version` · `invalid-params` · `release-from-driver`, from `ProtocolError::cause`, on the server's and the client's line alike, closed by `schemas/diag-line.v1.json`) and none on any other `channel-response` line, a refusal's included, whose own `detail` stays on `send-refused`. A hyprctl reply that is oversize or malformed gives one codes-only `parse-rejected{parser:"hyprctl-json"}` line, written by the Hyprland seam (never `unknown`). A StopFailure error word outside the CLI's 13 writes one WARN `parse-rejected{parser:"hook-stdin", detail:"unknown-value", count:1}` (code and count only) and the event is still delivered as a turn end with cause `api-error`; a known word writes no line.

record.title: Focus a session's window
record.requirement: `viola focus <name>` brings that session's window forward and switches to its workspace through Hyprland's own dispatch, by the identity recorded at `open`, or for a hand-started `viola run` by the wrapper's process ancestry; with none found it refuses with a named cause, and outside Hyprland it refuses `unsupported`
record.observed_gap: Finding the right window among about ten is the founder's own search; nothing in viola knows which window a session lives in.

verification.acceptance: Focusing a named live session brings its window forward on its workspace on Hyprland, for a session viola opened and for one started by hand, read live at R3 as `r3: green hand=focused opened=focused` in the chunk's evidence/r3.md, the active window after each focus being that session's terminal window. With no window found it refuses `window-not-found` (exit 1, no dispatch). With no `hyprctl` reachable it refuses `unsupported` (exit 1, nothing spawned); a host with `hyprctl` and no compositor answering refuses `unreachable`. The two refusals are proven over the fakes by `focus_with_no_window_of_its_session_is_window_not_found` and `focus_off_hyprland_is_unsupported`.
